papers.title: On the $d$-invariants of Brieskorn spheres and $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$
papers.abstract: We study the $d$-invariant from Heegaard Floer homology for Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(p,q,r)$. Using surgeries on two singular fibers, we establish new relations of the $d$-invariants among various Brieskorn spheres. For $p=2$, we show that $d$ never vanishes if $q/r$ lies in certain intervals on the rational line. Altogether, we completely classify Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(2,q,r)$ with $d=0$. The zero set is expressed using submonoids of $\mathrm{GL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ and the Stern--Brocot tree. As an application, we prove that most Brieskorn spheres $\Sigma(2,q,r)$ do not bound a rational homology $4$-ball.

papers.title: Localization of weighted Goldman volume on $\mathrm{SL}(3,\R)$-Hitchin Component
papers.abstract: We compute Goldman volume on the moduli space of convex real projective structures on a closed oriented surface of genus at least two, with exponential weight defined by the shifted Blaschke area. For every positive parameter, the integral converges and is a finite sum of inverse powers of that parameter. Its coefficients are intersection numbers involving the bundle of regular cubic differentials on the moduli stack of stable curves. The proof establishes absolute convergence and vanishing signed boundary integrals of the transgression under simultaneous plumbing degeneration. The pushforward of Goldman measure by the shifted Blaschke area therefore has a polynomial density on $[0,\infty)$, and its sublevel volumes are polynomial in the threshold.

papers.title: Unimodular random ideal hyperbolic polyhedra: geometric characteristics and random walks
papers.abstract: We initiate a systematic study of unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra in three-dimensional hyperbolic space, developing a geometric and probabilistic theory of their global behavior. At the heart of this theory is an intrinsic geometric characteristic, determined entirely by the dihedral angles surrounding a polyhedral face. We establish a unimodular Gauss-Bonnet identity and show that the expectation of this local geometric invariant completely determines the global conformal type: under suitable assumptions, a random ideal polyhedron is almost surely parabolic precisely when the expected characteristic vanishes, and hyperbolic precisely when it is negative. This provides a sharp geometric classification of random infinite ideal polyhedra. Building on the correspondence with ideal circle patterns, we further develop a refined Ring Lemma that yields quantitative geometric control without bounded-degree assumptions. Combining these geometric tools with unimodular probability methods, we identify the Poisson boundary of the face random walk and establish positive linear hyperbolic speed. Together, these results establish a local-to-global framework linking intrinsic dihedral geometry, conformal uniformization, and stochastic behavior at infinity for unimodular random infinite ideal hyperbolic polyhedra.

papers.title: Counting Markov triples and simple geodesics
papers.abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the number of Markov triples with largest entry below $x$. We show that the error term is $o(\log x)$, which improves upon the previous best known results due to McShane and Rivin. We give an explicit error based on classical zero-free regions of the Riemann zeta function, and a sharper estimate under the quasi-Riemann hypothesis. The proof uses the correspondence between Markov triples and simple closed geodesics on the modular punctured torus and a careful analysis of the McShane-Rivin unit ball.

papers.title: Recognizing convergence actions as proper isometric actions on hyperbolic spaces
papers.abstract: Relying merely on B.I. (a.k.a. Bowditch's intelligence), we show that whenever a group $G$ admits a convergence action on a compact perfect metrizable space $M$, there is a hyperbolic space $X$ along with a proper isometric action of $G$ on $X$ inducing a $G$-equivariant homeomorphism $f:M \rightarrow \partial X.$ This answers a question by Misha Kapovich.

papers.title: Filling knots and essential geodesic systole
papers.abstract: We prove that every closed, orientable $3$--manifold contains hyperbolic knots with arbitrarily large essential geodesic systole. That is, for any $3$--manifold $M$, and $R> 0$ there is a hyperbolic knot $K \subset M$ such that every closed geodesic in the knot complement which is non-null-homotopic in $M$ has length at least $R$. The construction also produces filling knots, in the sense of Freedman-Krushkal [FreeKrus2023]. This answers two questions of Biringer.

papers.title: The unknotting problem for surfaces in the 4-sphere
papers.abstract: We show that there is no algorithm to decide whether or not a closed, connected, orientable, locally flat PL surface in $S^4$ of genus at least 18 (resp. 19) is TOP (resp. PL) unknotted. We prove analogous results for non-orientable surfaces, and for surfaces in any compact PL 4-manifold. We also show that there is an orientable surface in $S^4$ of genus 18 whose group has unsolvable word problem, and an orientable surface in $S^4$ of genus 40 whose group contains an isomorphic copy of every recursively presented group. Similar results hold for non-orientable surfaces.

papers.title: Homological lifts of Arnold strangeness
papers.abstract: We construct homological lifts of Arnold's strangeness $\operatorname{St}$ for long and closed plane curves. For long curves, we introduce a new $q$-variable quantization polynomial $\operatorname{St}_q$, an edge state sum, designed for categorification and construct a triply graded homology that recovers $\operatorname{St}_q$. We prove strictness by exhibiting long curves with the same number of crossings and the same $\operatorname{St}_q$ (in particular, the same rotation number and $\operatorname{St}$) that are distinguished by the homology. For closed curves, we introduce a corresponding new polynomial $\operatorname{St}_q$ and construct an edge homology. In this case $\operatorname{St}_q$ is recovered from a signed $q$-character $\operatorname{ch}_q$ defined on the canonical cycles of the homology rather than directly from a graded rank. Again, we exhibit closed curves with the same number of crossings and the same $\operatorname{St}_q$ (in particular, the same rotation number and $\operatorname{St}$) that are distinguished by the homology.

papers.title: Three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations
papers.abstract: We show that if a three-manifold $M$ admits a veering triangulation, then the dual spine of every essential triangulation of $M$ can be smoothed to a branched surface. We use this criterion to identify a large collection of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds that do not admit veering triangulations. We then use the same criterion to construct the first infinite family of cusped hyperbolic three-manifolds without veering triangulations.

papers.title: Systolic pants decompositions with polynomial growth
papers.abstract: We investigate improved bounds on the kissing number of a hyperbolic surface under the assumption that the systole set contains pants decompositions with volume growth constraints. Namely, when the dual graph of the pants decomposition has polynomial volume growth, we obtain a power-savings improvement for the upper bound on the kissing number in terms of systolic length. We also construct super-exponentially many (in $g$) pants decompositions with exponential volume growth for which our techniques still imply stronger upper bounds for kissing numbers. The proofs use the technology of ``stem systems'' and ``tulips'' developed by the first and second author to study $1$-systems of curves.

papers.title: On Khovanov local equivalence groups
papers.abstract: Inspired by work in Seiberg--Witten and Heegaard Floer homology, Dunfield, Sch\"utz, and the author constructed an abelian "local equivalence group" built from pairs of chain complexes, and a homomorphism from the smooth concordance group to this group that uses the odd Khovanov complex and the Bar-Natan deformation of the even Khovanov complex. Lewark independently gave a related local equivalence group and concordance invariant, using only the Bar-Natan deformation. In this paper, we construct $(\mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z})^\infty$ subgroups of Lewark's local equivalence group and the kernel of the map from our local equivalence group to Lewark's, as well as $\mathbb{Z}^\infty$ direct summands of Lewark's group and this kernel, invisible to the $s$-invariants. The construction gives at least six $\mathbb{Z}$-valued concordance homomorphisms linearly independent from $s$, $\tau$, and Dai--Hom--Stoffregen--Truong's invariants.

papers.title: Counting Saddle Connections on Hyperelliptic Translation Surfaces with a Slit
papers.abstract: We consider saddle connections on a translation surface in a hyperelliptic connected component of a stratum that do not intersect the interior of a distinguished saddle connection. For this restricted set of saddle connections, we show that it satisfies an $L (\log L)^{d-2}$ growth rate, where $d$ is the complex dimension of the hyperelliptic stratum. The upper bound holds for all translation surfaces in the hyperelliptic stratum while the lower bound holds for almost every surface in the hyperelliptic stratum. The proof of the lower bound uses horocycle renormalization.

papers.title: Filling Links and Essential Systole
papers.abstract: We answer a question of Freedman and Krushkal, producing filling links in any closed, orientable 3-manifold. The links we construct are hyperbolic, and have large essential systole, contrasting earlier geometric constraints on hyperbolic links in 3-manifolds due to Adams-Reid and Lakeland-Leininger.

papers.title: Dehn quandles of surfaces and their bounded cohomology
papers.abstract: We introduce new families of quandles associated with closed orientable surfaces that can distinguish surfaces up to homeomorphism. These quandles generalize the classical Dehn quandle and are defined, respectively, on isotopy classes of unoriented essential closed curves and on integral weighted multicurves. We establish their fundamental algebraic properties and construct a natural quandle covering relating the two families. We further investigate their large-scale geometry and prove that they are unbounded with respect to the quandle metric. We determine their second bounded quandle cohomology and show that its dimension equals the cardinality of the continuum. We also establish a quandle-theoretic analogue of the Gromov Mapping Theorem, showing that the natural projection from an abelian quandle extension onto its base quandle induces an injection on bounded quandle cohomology in every degree. Finally, motivated by recent developments in quandle algebras, we study idempotents in the integral quandle algebras associated with the classical Dehn quandle. In particular, we prove that the integral quandle algebra of the Dehn quandle of the torus admits no non-trivial idempotents.

papers.title: Essential-Surface Complexes of Knot Exteriors: Image, Kernel, and Reconstruction
papers.abstract: This is an expository article. The curve complex of a surface is deliberately forgetful, yet in most cases its automorphism group recovers the mapping class group. We explain what happens when the same question is asked for the essential-surface complex $\mathcal{ES}(E)$ of a knot exterior $E=E(K)$, equivalently Schultens's initial surface complex $\mathcal{S}_0(E)$. The discussion is organized around three questions: which combinatorial symmetries are geometric (the image), which homeomorphisms are invisible (the kernel), and how much of $E$ can be read off from the complex (reconstruction). The basic objects are first drawn in classical examples, and the general framework is introduced only afterwards. We collect the elementary structural facts that organize the subject -- the flag property, the layering by boundary slope, finite dimension, unbounded dimension for iterated cables, and Kakimizu's complexes as full subcomplexes -- and compare with handlebodies and connected sums of $S^2\times S^1$, where image and kernel are known completely. Along the way we record two short consequences that we have not found stated in this form: for a slope-separated knot every orientation-preserving mapping class acts trivially, and the image is $\mathbb{Z}/2$ exactly when the knot is amphichiral and a nonzero boundary slope occurs; and for a connected sum of nonfibered prime knots the decomposing-annulus twist translates Banks's winding coordinate. A table separates what is classical from what is recorded here. The article closes with a three-task formulation of the rigidity problem, a list of problems with their current status, a worked two-bridge recipe, and a guide to further reading.
